hook.line: Don Hernando watches a bus at the corner. Did it just stop, or has it been standing there all morning? English says "stopped" for both, but Spanish makes you pick.
hook.es: El bus se paró en la esquina.
hook.en: The bus stopped at the corner.

examples.es: La máquina se detuvo de repente.
El bus se paró en la esquina.
examples.en: The bus stopped at the corner.

examples.es: El carro estaba parado en el semáforo.
examples.en: The car was stopped at the lights.

examples.es: Los obreros estaban parados frente al edificio.
examples.en: The workers were standing in front of the building.

examples.es: Don Hernando se detuvo frente a la puerta.
examples.en: Don Hernando stopped in front of the door.

rule:
Two different things.

The moment of stopping: *se detuvo*, *se paró*. *Detenerse* is a little more formal; *pararse* is everyday.

The state afterwards: *estaba parado*, *estaba quieto*. This word agrees with what is stopped: *los carros estaban parados*, *ella estaba parada*. In Latin America *estar parado* also means standing up.

To ask someone to hold still: *quédate quieto* (friend), *quédese quieto* (usted).
smallPrint: Teachers call *se detuvo* an event and *estaba parado* a resulting state: *estar* plus a participle, as in *está cerrado*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *se paró* or *estaba parado* and type the whole sentence: *El bus ___ en la esquina.* (The bus stopped at the corner.)
yourTurn.answer: El bus se paró en la esquina.
yourTurn.why: A single moment of stopping is an event: *se paró*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: The car was stopped at the lights.
yourTurn.answer: El carro estaba parado en el semáforo.
yourTurn.why: Being stopped is a state, so *estaba parado*, with no *se*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: The machine suddenly stopped.
yourTurn.answer: La máquina se detuvo de repente.
yourTurn.why: The moment it stopped is an event: *se detuvo*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: The cars were stopped in the street.
yourTurn.answer: Los carros estaban parados en la calle.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: Keep still.
yourTurn.why: *Quédate quieto* is how you ask a friend to hold still.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it politely to a stranger (usted): Keep still, please.
Type in Spanish: Don Hernando stopped in front of the door.
yourTurn.answer: Don Hernando se detuvo frente a la puerta.
yourTurn.why: He stopped at one moment, so *se detuvo*.

pitfalls.wrong: El carro se estaba parado en el semáforo.
pitfalls.right: El carro estaba parado en el semáforo.
pitfalls.why: Almost. Being stopped is a state, so drop *se* and keep *estaba parado*.

pitfalls.wrong: Los carros estaban parado en la calle.
pitfalls.right: Los carros estaban parados en la calle.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Parado* agrees with the cars, so it takes the plural ending.

pitfalls.wrong: Ella se paró junto a la puerta toda la tarde.
pitfalls.right: Ella estuvo parada junto a la puerta toda la tarde.
pitfalls.why: Almost. For a state that lasted, use *estar parado*; *se paró* is just the moment she stopped or stood up.

personal: Say something true about a place you know: what stopped there, or what is stopped there right now.
